There are actually not many software limitations when switching from Windows to Mac. Not only can all the largest PC applications run on this platform, but there are also countless practical applications exclusive to Mac.

The biggest exception is games. However, the latest tests show that, whether through official or unofficial means, Windows games perform better on Mac than ever before……

Apple has an exclusive game porting toolkit to help developers evaluate how their Windows games will run on Mac. The aim is to encourage and facilitate them in porting games to the Mac platform.

However, as Filipe Esposito of 《Macworld》 mentioned, this toolkit is also used by gamers to unofficially run Windows software on Mac. He himself is one of them, and pointed out that the latest beta version has brought significant performance improvements, citing 《Grand Theft Auto V》 as an example.

After spending several days testing Game Porting Toolkit 4 beta on a MacBook Pro equipped with M4 Pro, he found that the performance improvements fundamentally changed the experience of running demanding Windows games……On the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, with the same game settings and the same benchmark, the frame rate of 《GTA V》 increased from about 106 fps on GPTK 3 to about 176 fps on GPTK 4 beta, an increase of approximately 66%. The game runs quite smoothly at medium-to-high quality settings at 2K resolution.

He acknowledged that not every game has such dramatic improvements, but hopes these improvements will encourage game studios to see Mac as a viable platform.
